about.statement: I build software end to end — the database, the APIs, the web and mobile UI, the ML models and the deployment. Mostly that means *multi-tenant SaaS* that stays fast, secure and properly isolated, and AI features that cite their sources instead of making things up.
body: At **Siga Infotech** (since June 2024) I build and run multi-tenant SaaS platforms for restaurants, UK care homes, staffing agencies, retail and AI — about a thousand commits across fourteen production repositories — and look after the AWS production setup they run on, down to the monthly bill.

On my own time I trained a graph neural network from scratch to forecast India's air quality, built a knowledge-graph learning app that refuses to hallucinate, an app that turns an Android phone into a PC microphone, and a studio that turns GitHub activity into animated art. I think about failure modes first, and I quite enjoy the hard migrations nobody else wants.

projects.title: Breathe

form.name: gnn-india
form.caption: Twenty-nine Indian cities as a graph. The light running along the edges is message passing — each city learning from its neighbours’ air.

projects.summary: Forecasts India's air quality with a graph neural network I trained from scratch — running on the server and on the phone.
description: Breathe forecasts air quality for India and helps people plan healthier trips. It's a Flutter app, a React web app, a React ML-ops console, a NestJS API and a Python inference service — about 43k lines in total.

The heart of it is a GCN-Transformer-GRU spatio-temporal graph neural network over 29 Indian cities and 569 distance-weighted edges. I distilled a 4.86M-parameter teacher into a 491K-parameter student — about 10× smaller — and the student actually beat the teacher on the held-out test set.
highlights: Forecasts PM2.5, PM10 and NO₂ an hour ahead from a 48-hour window of 14 features per city; overall R² 0.945, PM2.5 MAE 4.5 µg/m³.
Exported to ONNX (1.58 MB) with a parity check, served from FastAPI **and on-device in Flutter** — I rewrote the feature pipeline in Dart to match the Python training pipeline exactly.
MLOps: live drift evaluation against real readings every 6 hours, a model version registry and an admin dashboard with an SVG city graph.
Self-hosted OSRM on the whole-India road graph; alternative routes ranked by AQI sampled along each route, plus a hand-written PDF carbon report.
Refresh-token rotation with reuse detection that revokes every session, Redis deny-lists, and a startup check that refuses unsafe production config.

projects.title: PhoneInput

form.name: phone-wave
form.caption: 10 ms Opus frames leaving the phone, through an adaptive jitter buffer, into a virtual microphone on the desktop.

projects.summary: Turns an Android phone into a low-latency microphone for Windows and Linux — over Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth — that Discord, Zoom and OBS can pick like any other mic.
description: The phone captures and cleans up the audio, compresses it with Opus and streams it to a desktop app, which plays it into a virtual microphone. The computer can stream its own audio back, so the phone doubles as a speaker.

One Kotlin Multiplatform module shares the wire protocol, jitter buffer, noise suppressor and Compose design system between the phone and desktop apps — about 10,000 lines and 45 unit tests, taken from an empty folder to v1.1.2 with installers and auto-update in two days.
highlights: A custom UDP audio protocol: 10 ms frames of 48 kHz audio, Opus at 96 kbit/s in low-delay mode, and an **adaptive jitter buffer** (30–250 ms) sized from measured jitter, with packet-loss concealment and fade-outs instead of hard cuts.
Three transports: LAN discovery and QR pairing, USB through TCP-framed `adb reverse`, and Bluetooth RFCOMM over native sockets via JNA — Winsock `AF_BTH` on Windows, BlueZ on Linux.

**No echo in screen shares:** a probe tone showed process loopback leaking the voice into Discord Go Live and OBS at −17.7 dBFS, so the virtual mic is written through WASAPI exclusive mode to bypass the Windows mixer.
Phone as speaker: desktop audio streams back in stereo Opus at 128 kbit/s, captured by process loopback of every app except PhoneInput itself.
Up to 8 phones at once, guided VB-CABLE and PipeWire/PulseAudio setup, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that ships APK, MSI/EXE, DEB and RPM with SHA-256-verified auto-updates.

projects.title: FloatPro

form.name: receipt
form.caption: An ESC/POS receipt. The Flutter POS finds printers over Bluetooth and mDNS and prints from templates.

projects.summary: A multi-tenant restaurant platform for the UK — I designed its permission system, billing, compliance, AI assistant and much of the Flutter POS.
description: FloatPro (also sold as Zynk and EasyDine) is a TypeScript backend on AWS Lambda, a tenant admin portal, a super-admin console and a Flutter waiter / POS / KDS app running on Android, Windows and iMin hardware. I've made about 690 commits across its four repositories.

I designed the PAC (Permission-Action-Control) authorization system, built the subscription and billing layer, the food-safety compliance module and the HR/payroll suite, and led the phased migration from the Express monolith to NestJS 11.
highlights: **AI assistant:** a 4-layer multi-agent text-to-SQL pipeline — an orchestrator routing to SQL/UI/general agents, a validator that only allows a single read-only SELECT, execution inside `BEGIN READ ONLY`, and reversible PII masking in Redis.
**PAC authorization:** a DB-driven route registry, subscription-tier module sync with repair logic, per-user PLUS/MINUS overrides and Redis permission caching.
**API key gateway:** per-tenant vaulted secrets, HMAC pepper rotation, Redis Lua sliding-window rate limiting, IP allow/block lists and step-up re-auth.

**Flutter POS:** a Dio interceptor chain with single-flight token refresh, an ESC/POS printing subsystem with Bluetooth/mDNS discovery and templates, and a CI/CD pipeline producing signed, auto-versioned builds delivered to OneDrive.
**HR suite:** about 30k lines of frontend across people, time, pay and documents — including a config-driven form engine and an ID-card print engine.

projects.title: README Templates

form.name: black-hole
form.caption: Singularity, one of the seven templates: a particle per day of contributions, falling into a black hole. On GitHub it’s a plain SVG animated with CSS.

projects.summary: A desktop studio that turns your GitHub activity into original, animated artwork for your profile README — then publishes it to your profile in one commit.
description: Generators hand you a block of markdown and leave the rest to you, and the usual stats cards come from third-party services that get rate-limited and look the same on every profile. README Templates does the whole job: pick a template, connect GitHub, edit the text against a preview that matches GitHub in dark and light, and publish.
Every image is a plain SVG committed to your own repo — nothing depends on an outside service, so nothing breaks later. It runs entirely on your machine: no server, no sign-up, no analytics.
highlights: Seven templates, each a data visualisation dressed as a scene — a black hole with one particle per day of contributions, a reef with one coral per week, a dusk city with one tower per day.

Animated with **CSS keyframes inside the SVG** so it survives GitHub's `` tag — no GIFs, no JavaScript, no SMIL — and the resting state is always the final frame, so reduced-motion viewers see the finished picture.

Tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from a **non-extractable WebCrypto key**, a CSP that only allows the app and `api.github.com`, no file-read capability, and a Rust guard that sends every outside link to the system browser.
Tauri v2 instead of Electron: a ~3 MB installer, NSIS/MSI and deb/rpm/AppImage builds, and a signed auto-updater released by a tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow.
Animations tested headlessly — forced reduced-motion screenshots for the final frame, then filmstrips seeked through `document.getAnimations()` to catch timing bugs.

projects.title: AI Hub

form.name: embeddings
form.caption: Retrieval without a framework: embeddings in pgvector, a query, and its five nearest neighbours by cosine.

projects.summary: A modular AI platform — content generation, document extraction, résumé scoring and a RAG chatbot — on which I was nearly the sole developer.
description: AI Hub covers text, SEO, code, social, image and video generation, schema-based document extraction, ATS résumé analysis and a knowledge-base chatbot, served through a customer portal, an admin portal and a public API.

I hand-built the RAG pipeline with no framework, the moderation and strike system, and a credit-wallet billing engine — then ported the whole backend from Express/Drizzle to NestJS/TypeORM with the API contract preserved, and designed a Python control plane for v2.
highlights: **RAG:** gemini-embedding-001 vectors in pgvector via a custom TypeORM transformer, sliding-window chunking, top-k cosine search over active entries, and human review of extracted knowledge.
**Billing:** a three-bucket wallet (plan → prepaid → pay-as-you-go) with pre-auth holds and `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` locking, Stripe Checkout and idempotent webhooks.
**Port:** about 17.6k LOC and 143 routes moved to NestJS; a schema-parity checker confirmed 41/41 tables and 493/493 columns — and caught three latent billing bugs.
**v2 control plane (Python):** a 7-step resumable provisioning state machine, PgBouncer routing, Ed25519 JWT/JWKS, an SSRF-safe HTTP client and 532 tests against real Postgres servers.
A WebGL landing page with custom GLSL shaders, post-processing and Lenis scrollytelling.

projects.title: OG Converter

form.name: wheel
form.caption: Start dragging a file, tap Shift, Ctrl or Alt, and a radial menu opens at the cursor.

projects.summary: A fully offline Windows file converter: start dragging a file, tap a key, and drop it on a radial menu that opens at the cursor.
description: OG Converter converts, compresses, edits and encrypts files without opening an app. While you drag a file from File Explorer or a VS Code-style editor, tapping Shift, Ctrl or Alt opens a Convert, Tools or Actions wheel, and the result is saved next to the original. Nothing is uploaded.

It's a native tray app in C#, .NET 10 and WPF — about 19k lines across ~90 files — that routes each job to FFmpeg, Windows imaging codecs, Office over COM, LibreOffice, headless Edge or managed code, running heavy work in short-lived separate processes.
highlights: Detects the gesture inside another app's drag with **low-level Win32 keyboard and mouse hooks**, and finds the dragged file through Shell COM interfaces in Explorer and **UI Automation** in VS Code-based editors.
Lossless and lossy compression for 10+ file families: TinyPNG-style palette quantization, two-pass target-size video and **automatic GPU encoder detection** (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF).
A custom `.ogx` encrypted container with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 and Argon2id key derivation, plus AES-256 protection for PDF and Office files.
A plugin system for wheel renderers loaded into a collectible `AssemblyLoadContext`, five built-in themes with synthesized sound packs, and a no-code JSON template format.
A built-in `--test` suite with pixel-level lossless checks and encryption round-trips, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that publishes a checksummed single-file exe.

projects.title: ClinicFlow

form.name: hash-chain
form.caption: Medical records as an append-only ledger: every entry carries the SHA-256 hash of the one before it.

projects.summary: A WhatsApp-first clinic queue for Kerala — patients book by chatting in English or Malayalam, and the waiting room watches the queue move live.
description: ClinicFlow is a multi-tenant SaaS for clinics. Patients book through a bilingual WhatsApp chatbot; the clinic runs a live token queue that also shows on a waiting-room TV board.
Under the hood: 15 domain modules, 75 REST endpoints and 23 entities, covered by 80 end-to-end tests, with medical records kept in an append-only, hash-chained ledger.
highlights: A bilingual booking state machine on WhatsApp interactive lists and buttons — with consent, opt-out and 24-hour-window rules — and **automatic failover to Telegram** via a ports-and-adapters design.
Live queue on Socket.IO rooms per tenant and per doctor, wait times from a rolling average of recent consultations, and proactive "your turn is coming" alerts.
Append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained medical records; external labs upload via API key, and reports are delivered through signed, expiring, PIN-protected links.
DPDPA 2023 data export and erasure, per-clinic roles, audited super-admin impersonation behind TOTP MFA, and PostgreSQL row-level security.
Razorpay subscriptions verified with HMAC, with dunning from Active → Past Due → booking-only mode.

projects.title: Easy Learn

form.name: knowledge-graph
form.caption: Every node keeps the passage it came from. If the quote isn’t in the source, the node never reaches the graph.

projects.summary: Turns study material into an interactive knowledge graph where every node can be traced back to the exact passage it came from.
description: Easy Learn ingests PDFs, Word files, Markdown, HTML, CSV, JSON and images, plus AI study chats, and turns them into a graph you can explore by focus, timeline or search.
The rule I designed it around: the LLM must quote its source, and nothing reaches the graph until a person approves it.
highlights: An ingestion state machine — extract → chunk → structure with the LLM → dedupe → review — with per-format extractors that record exactly where each passage came from.
**Hallucination guard:** a node is rejected unless its quote appears in the source chunk (normalised substring or fuzzy ratio ≥ 0.85); approved quotes are stored with a SHA-256 hash.
Duplicate detection from embedding cosine similarity plus title similarity, with versioned node history.
OpenAI and Gemini behind one interface with an automatic fallback chain, bring-your-own-key with Fernet encryption, and rule-based fallbacks when no LLM is available.
Hybrid full-text + pgvector search, an offline PWA caching the graph in IndexedDB, Stripe subscriptions and SSE progress streaming.

projects.title: CareRez

form.name: db-tenants
form.caption: Database-per-tenant: created at runtime, resolved by subdomain, kept warm in an LRU of fifty.

projects.summary: A platform for UK residential care providers. I wrote its first commit, designed its database-per-tenant architecture and moved it to serverless.
description: CareRez is organised as Company → Homes → Units → Residents and Staff, across an Express/TypeScript backend, a React admin portal, a super-admin console and two Flutter apps.
I founded the backend codebase and was its top committer (243 of 757 commits) — the multi-tenancy, auth and RBAC framework, clinical and finance modules and the SaaS control plane.
highlights: Database-per-tenant on Sequelize: runtime DB creation, subdomain resolution, and a `DBFactory` with LRU eviction (50 active domains), idle cleanup, health checks and request-scoped instances.
A declarative route-auth map compiled with path-to-regexp, with AND/OR role and permission checks behind a type-safe API.
Clinical modules: the medicine master, resident medication slots and **MAR sheet APIs**, treatments with follow-ups and inventory batches.
A resident finance ledger with budget limits, reserve funds with reversal entries and DB-transaction-wrapped operations.
Serverless with AWS CDK: ARM64 Lambda, API Gateway with X-Ray and a TLS-only policy, webpack → esbuild, and a GitHub Actions deploy pipeline.

projects.title: Zynk Suite
projects.summary: A multi-tenant platform for UK temporary-staffing agencies with five user tiers — I bootstrapped the platform and own the client domain.
description: Zynk Suite (Sqube) serves system admins, super admins, agency admins, staff and client-portal users. I bootstrapped it from our multi-tenant SaaS core and removed about 17k lines of the old restaurant domain.
highlights: Capacity-aware tenant placement on a DB-server registry, `CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE` provisioning and a reviewable schema-diff migration-job system.
A multi-user Client Portal identity model: per-device sessions storing only refresh-token hashes, rotation with a multi-tab grace window, and per-request branch scoping cached in Redis.
Jobs, booking calendar, holiday pay and timesheet sign-off; a compliance-minded archive with a nine-rule eligibility engine.
Migrated the staff portal from Next.js 14 to Vite — 2,564 files, kept working through a Next.js compatibility shim.

projects.title: Subscription Service
projects.summary: One app-agnostic subscription and billing service shared by many products and tenants — proration, dues, tax-aware invoicing and churn analytics.
description: I built v1 on Express, migrated it to NestJS 11 within two weeks with a use-case-driven clean architecture, and then took it through nine months of production hardening. Primary author: 22 of 24 commits, about 9,200 lines.
highlights: Mid-cycle proration with two credit strategies — refund, or bonus days at the new plan's daily rate — using integer-cents arithmetic.
A bill-preview engine that runs the same maths as the real operation and returns warnings, minimum and recommended payments before anyone commits.
Oldest-first dues settlement, GST/VAT-style tax snapshots, freeze/unfreeze, and an hourly expiry cron that switches to an HTTP trigger in serverless deployments.
SaaS analytics: revenue, ARPT, churn, retention, tenant risk scoring and renewal-pattern classification.

projects.title: Siga POS
projects.summary: A retail and inventory POS with one database per tenant — I built its loyalty engine and GST compliance reporting.
description: Siga POS is a Flutter app on an Express/Drizzle backend with separate master and tenant configs.
highlights: A loyalty program engine: tiered credit rules with range-overlap validation and memberships that can be purchased, upgraded, redeemed and expired.
GSTR-1, GSTR-2 and GSTR-3B reports with JSON, PDF and Excel export.
A barcode-scanner POS overlay, desktop features (service charges, manager PIN, tax-inclusive pricing) and wastage and near-expiry reports.

projects.title: PropSure
projects.summary: A property-verification platform and real-estate CRM for Kerala — shipped by me alone, from first commit to production with full observability.
description: PropSure scores properties against a configurable inspection checklist ("Know Before You Buy"), publishes verified listings, captures enquiries as CRM leads and manages pipelines and site visits — about 51k lines of TypeScript across a NestJS API, a React admin portal and a trilingual marketing site.
highlights: A weighted two-level verification scoring engine as pure, unit-tested functions that re-scores affected properties when the rules change.
Admin auth with a TOTP authenticator implemented from RFC 6238, AES-256-GCM encrypted secrets, Redis session rotation and per-IP lockout.
A partner API platform: scoped keys stored as SHA-256 hashes, BigInt CIDR matching and Redis rate limiting with automatic blocking.
GitHub Actions CD with health-gated rollout and automatic rollback, and the full Grafana LGTM stack with trace ↔ log ↔ metric correlation.

projects.title: PropSure LMS
projects.summary: An enterprise lead-management CRM on Spring Boot where every customer company gets its own physically isolated database.
description: A Gradle multi-module modular monolith (12 modules, 46 endpoints) with a React 19 frontend: a dark control plane for platform admins and a light workspace for six tenant roles.
highlights: Database-per-tenant via `AbstractRoutingDataSource`, Caffeine-cached HikariCP pools per tenant and a staged provisioning pipeline (create DB → Flyway → seed → activate).
RBAC with six roles plus row-level data security through JPA Criteria specifications.
Lead scoring with MQL/SQL qualification, Jaro-Winkler duplicate detection, conversion to accounts and opportunities, and round-robin assignment.
Real-time collaboration on WebSocket/STOMP: presence, edit locks and threaded comments with @mentions.

projects.title: FleetBooks
projects.summary: A fleet-finance app for vehicle-hire businesses — one React Native codebase running on Android, iOS and the web.
description: FleetBooks covers client receivables, drivers, vehicles, odometer readings, attendance and daily allowances, delivered spec-first: user stories, derived requirements and implementation plans with risk analysis.
highlights: A hand-written Vite config that bundles React Native for the browser (migrated from Webpack).
A responsive shell — sidebar on desktop, bottom bar and drawer on mobile — kept in sync through a global navigation reference.
A token-based design system (34 Material-3 colour roles) and 26 components, including charts built from plain views.

projects.title: Engineering Playbooks
projects.summary: My production lessons on multi-tenancy and permissions, packaged as skills that AI coding agents load and follow.
description: Two reusable playbooks: `multitenancy` (all three isolation strategies with 12 NestJS templates) and `pac`, a ~7.7k-line permission engine combining RBAC, PBAC and ABAC.
highlights: Trusted-source tenant resolution, AsyncLocalStorage context and how jobs and webhooks re-establish tenant scope.
DENY-always-wins permission evaluation with O(1) lookups, full PostgreSQL DDL and a catalogue of 26 design decisions, each with the failure it prevents.
